binders: m and n are arbitrary natural numbers, possibly zero.
A is an arbitrary real m-by-n matrix, represented as A(i,j) for i in Fin m and j in Fin n.
DeltaA is an arbitrary real-parameterized family of m-by-n real matrices.
For each column j in Fin n, columnRemainder(j) is a real-valued function of u.
c6 is a natural number and lambda is a real number.
hypotheses: For every j in Fin n, columnRemainder(j,u) = O(u^2) as u tends to 0 through values in (0,1). The big-O constant may depend on j and on the fixed data.
For all sufficiently small positive u, simultaneously for every j in Fin n, ||DeltaA(u)[:,j]||_2 <= beta(u) ||A[:,j]||_2 + |columnRemainder(j,u)|.
conclusions: There exists a real-valued function normwiseRemainder such that normwiseRemainder(u) = O(u^2) as u tends to 0 through values in (0,1).
For all sufficiently small positive u, ||DeltaA(u)||_F <= beta(u) ||A||_F + |normwiseRemainder(u)|.
mathematical_definitions: For x indexed by Fin m, ||x||_2 = sqrt(sum_{i in Fin m} x_i^2).
For an m-by-n matrix B, ||B||_F = sqrt(sum_{i in Fin m} sum_{j in Fin n} B(i,j)^2).
g_m,lambda(u) = exp((lambda * sqrt(m) * u + m * u^2)/(1-u)) - 1.
beta(u) = c6 * lambda * sqrt(n) * g_m,lambda(u), where c6, m, and n are cast to reals.
An eventual assertion at nhdsWithin(0,(0,1)) means that it holds for every sufficiently small u satisfying 0 < u < 1.
The assertion r(u) = O(u^2) on this filter means that some constant C bounds |r(u)| by C|u^2| for all sufficiently small positive u.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Fix arbitrary finite matrix dimensions m and n, a real matrix A, a real matrix-valued perturbation DeltaA(u), one remainder function for each column, a positive natural constant c6, and a positive real lambda. Define beta(u) = c6 lambda sqrt(n) [exp((lambda sqrt(m) u + m u^2)/(1-u)) - 1]. Assume every column remainder is O(u^2) as u approaches zero from the right within (0,1), and assume that on one common sufficiently small positive neighborhood of zero every column of DeltaA(u) has Euclidean norm at most beta(u) times the corresponding column norm of A plus the absolute value of that column's remainder. Then there exists a single real function that is O(u^2) on the same one-sided limiting filter and whose absolute value completes the analogous bound for the Frobenius norm of the whole matrix.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimensions are unrestricted natural numbers. If n=0, all column quantifiers are vacuous and both Frobenius norms are zero; the conclusion can be satisfied by a zero remainder.
If m=0, every column norm and both Frobenius norms are zero, so the displayed inequalities reduce to nonnegativity of absolute values and carry no matrix information.
All asymptotic and inequality statements are local and one-sided: they concern only sufficiently small u with 0 < u < 1, exclude u=0, and impose nothing away from zero.
The columnwise eventual hypothesis uses one common sufficiently small neighborhood for all columns, rather than a separately chosen neighborhood for each column.
The individual big-O constants for the column remainders are not stated to be equal or uniform, although the finite column index set permits finite aggregation.
The existential normwise remainder is not defined in terms of the supplied column remainders and is not required to equal any particular combination of them.
No sign condition is imposed on any remainder function; only its absolute value is used in an inequality.
No entrywise relation, matrix equation, algorithmic origin, or structural relationship between A and DeltaA is encoded beyond the stated norm bounds.
The result is an absolute norm bound, not a relative error statement, and no nonzero assumption is imposed on A or its columns.
The hidden big-O constants and the sufficiently small neighborhoods may depend on all fixed parameters and functions.
The parameter c6 is restricted to positive natural numbers rather than arbitrary positive real constants.
